title: Feasibility study of a lifestyle app for evaluating digital, adaptive nutrition recommendations under everyday conditions
summary:
Food affects every person differently. The same food can make one person tired, give another energy, or cause abdominal pain in a third person with a sensitive gut. Even in the same person, the reaction can fluctuate from day to day. Nevertheless, most previous nutritional recommendations are very general and do not precisely fit the individual person. Yet this would be particularly important, since well-being and health often depend heavily on food. Previous ways of getting personally suitable recommendations are usually very time-consuming: keeping diaries for weeks, doing blood tests, or wearing bothersome measuring devices. This is expensive and hardly sustainable in everyday life. Moreover, these recommendations are then usually based only on a brief snapshot and cannot respond to changes within a person over a longer period of time.

We are testing a simple digital program. It collects the information you enter (e.g., how you feel or what you eat) as well as the data transmitted via connected wearables such as fitness trackers or smartwatches. Based on this data, the program continually adapts its nutritional recommendations. This way, you can find out without much effort which nutrition personally suits you. The study examines whether this approach works in everyday life and whether users like using it. It is not about medical treatment, but about a practical everyday aid.
conditions: Healthy study participants and individuals with subdiagnostic gastrointestinal complaints (do not meet Rome IV criteria / do not meet the criteria for a relevant ICD-10 diagnosis); Prevention of functional gastrointestinal complaints in healthy adults and promotion and maintenance of a healthy lifestyle

interventions.name: Healthy study participants: 28-day use of a lifestyle application to assess the usability of digitally delivered adaptive nutritional recommendations.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-Age 18 to 70 years
-BMI 18.5 to 30 kg/m²
-Sufficient knowledge of German
-Capacity to consent and informed consent
-Possession of a suitable iOS or Android smartphone
-Confident handling of the smartphone
-Willingness to actively use the app over 28 days
-Willingness to document nutrition and symptoms (in case of gastrointestinal complaints)
-Willingness and ability to use one's own compatible wearable or a provided study wearable.
Exclusion criteria:
-Pregnancy, planned pregnancy during the study period, or breastfeeding
-Participation in another study involving a digital application or nutritional intervention
-Acute or untreated illness requiring treatment
-Current or past eating disorder
-Severe untreated mental illness
-Relevant organic disease or warning signs of such a disease (alarm signs)
-Other circumstances that, in the assessment of the study management, make safe or meaningful participation impossible
